title: Paradigmes des courbes algébriques (version provisoire) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. Section 7 of these notes builds a dictionary for the arithmetic fundamental group of a curve. One side is an extension 1→π→E→G→1, for example geometric π1 → arithmetic π1 → Galois group. The other side is a fundamental groupoid with a G-action. The previous page introduces two categories. C consists of systems (1→π→E→G→1, Z), where Z is a nonempty E-set on which π acts freely; in the motivating case Z is a set of points of a universal cover X̃'(J) lying over a set J of base points. C' consists of systems (Π, Π̃, p, G, u), where Π is a connected groupoid, p: Π̃→Π is a universal covering, and u: G→Aut(Π) is a strict action by automorphisms. This page constructs the functor α: C→C'; the next page constructs the quasi-inverse β.

Step 1, the groupoid Π. Put J = Z/π, the set of π-orbits. Each orbit Z_j is a π-torsor. Define Ob Π = J and Hom(j,j') = Isom_π(Z_j, Z_j'), with the obvious composition. Π is connected because any two π-torsors are isomorphic. Its vertex groups are Aut_π(Z_j), which is (anti-)isomorphic to π.

Step 2, the covering Π̃. Put Ob Π̃ = Z and let Hom(z,z') be a single point for every z, z'. So Π̃ is the indiscrete (codiscrete) groupoid on Z: connected and simply connected. The functor p sends z to its orbit z̄. It sends the unique arrow z→z' to the unique π-equivariant isomorphism Z_z̄ → Z_z̄' taking z to z'; this exists and is unique because the orbits are torsors.

Step 3, Π̃ as a covering. Grothendieck recasts Π̃ as the discrete fibration ("catégorie discrète sur Π") attached to the functor F(j) = Z_j, that is, Π̃ ≃ Π/F, the category of elements of F. Choosing z0 ∈ Z_j0 gives Isom_π(Z_j0, Z_j) ≅ Z_j via f ↦ f(z0). So F is representable, which is exactly why Π/F is the universal cover.

Step 4, using E. So far E has not been used. E acts on Z, hence by automorphisms on the indiscrete groupoid Π̃, since every permutation of the objects of an indiscrete groupoid is an automorphism. The subgroup π acts by deck transformations over Π: if f is π-equivariant with f(z)=z', then f(γz) = γz'. Hence G = E/π acts on Π ≅ Π̃/π by passing to the quotient.

Explicitly, e ∈ E sends Z_j to Z_{ej}, because π is normal, and sends f to e∘f∘e⁻¹, which is again π-equivariant. An element γ ∈ π acts by f ↦ γfγ⁻¹ = f, so it acts trivially on Π. The resulting G-action on Π is therefore strict, not merely an outer action, and it is compatible with the E-action on Π̃.

What it serves. This turns the classical outer action G→Out(π) into a genuine action on a groupoid with many base points J. Inertia and cusp data (T ≅ Ẑ(1), the character χ, and Φ: C→Hom(T,π)) are then transported to this setting on the next page (§8).
errors: Π̃ is called a 'cat. discrète', but with all Hom-sets singletons it is the indiscrete (codiscrete) groupoid on Z. 'Discrète sur Π' must be read as 'discrete fibration over Π', which is correct.
F is written as F: Π°→Ens, yet the transport maps Isom_π(Z_j, Z_j') act covariantly on the Z_j. This variance slip is harmless because Π is a groupoid.
The page only sketches why E acts on Π̃ compatibly and why π acts trivially on Π. These checks are easy and true (π acts trivially since morphisms are π-equivariant), but they are left implicit.
Vertex groups are Aut_π(Z_j), which is canonically identified only with the opposite group of π, or with π after choosing a point. This is a convention issue, not addressed on the page.

ideas.what: Connected groupoid Π on the orbit set Z/π, with morphisms the π-torsor isomorphisms between orbits.
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groupoid with many base points; groupoid of torsors (orbit groupoid).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Brandt/Higgins/R. Brown for the groupoid formalism; Grothendieck (SGA1) for fundamental groupoids of fibre functors.
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. V (fundamental groupoid); Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche (many base points).

ideas.what: The universal cover of Π realised as the indiscrete groupoid on Z, i.e. the category of elements of the representable functor j ↦ Z_j.
ideas.modern_name: Universal covering groupoid as category of elements of a representable functor; covering ↔ discrete fibration ↔ Π-set.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Gabriel–Zisman, R. Brown, Topology and Groupoids).

ideas.what: Equivalence between (extension 1→π→E→G→1 plus E-set Z with free π-action) and (connected groupoid with universal cover plus strict G-action). This rigidifies an outer action into a strict groupoid action, with E recovered as automorphisms of Π̃ lifting G.
ideas.modern_name: Extensions as group actions on groupoids; E ≅ vertex group of the semidirect groupoid Π ⋊ G; Galois action on the fundamental groupoid.
ideas.usually_credited_to: R. Brown, Higgins (groupoid semidirect products/orbit groupoids); used arithmetically by Deligne 1989, Ihara, Nakamura.
ideas.where_published: Spirit present in La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981, published 2022 edition); exact formulation unsure.

deep.surprise_reason: A correct, routine categorical translation of group extensions with a free E-set into strict G-actions on a connected groupoid with universal cover. It is standard groupoid theory and part of Grothendieck's known 'many base points' philosophy; nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: '(ens[?] 𝒥[?])' should read '(soit J)', i.e. Ob Π = Z/π =: J.
'Isom(z,z') = {k}' probably means a one-point set ('{pt}'): Π̃ is the indiscrete groupoid.
'π opère par Π automorphismes' should be 'π opère par Π-automorphismes', i.e. automorphisms over Π (deck transformations).
'par principes ... quotients' is most likely 'par passage au quotient'.
The line '[-sur-] sur Π' near the top-right box reads 'Π̃ cat. discrète sur Π définie par un foncteur F: Π°→Ens'; the margin note beside the first brace reads 'd'un groupoïde Π'.
